nar.text: Campari's number 2 Alfa Romeo was first to be sent off and Foresti's number 4 Bugatti followed at 8:03 AM.
Campari's number 2 Alfa Romeo was first to be sent off and Foresti's number 4 Bugatti followed at 8:03 AM.
Minoia leads after the first lap in a record 1h25m17s.
Borzacchini in second place also broke the record in 1h25m21s at 75.922 km/h, likewise third placed Brilli Peri in 1h25m45s, followed by Divo half a minute behind.
The eighth placed Wagner lost time changing a punctured tire on his Bugatti.
Conelli made a three minute refueling stop, his time was 1h32m37s.
Ernesto Maserati retires at Collesano with a broken magneto drive.
In the cyclecar class Biondetti leads; Fagioli's Salmson retires.

The independent Swiss retired at the pits with several broken valve springs on his Bugatti.

He offered to take over, jumped into the car and continued the race.

Brilli Peri and Campari both stopped at the pits for fuel and new wheels, while Borzacchini passed the finish at speed.
Conelli's Bugatti hits a rock that has rolled onto the road, damaging a fuel line; he repairs it on the road.

When Borzacchini retired his Maserati with a broken rear axle crown wheel only two miles from the finish, Campari gained fourth place
Divo wins; Minoia is second and Brilli Peri third, with Campari fourth.
Lepori, who had taken over Bittman's Bugatti finished in fifth position but was disqualified because relief drivers had to be nominated before the start.
